sentence: The expenses accounted for nearly half of the total budget
explanation: 'Account for' significa representar una proporción. Pasado simple en una afirmación de hecho.

sentence: She needs to brush up on her French before the trip
hint: Third person singular: needs to + base form
explanation: 'Brush up on' significa repasar y mejorar. Con 'she', se usa 'needs', no 'need'.

sentence: We cannot do without reliable internet in the modern workplace
explanation: 'Do without' significa arreglárselas sin algo. 'Cannot' + forma base para expresar imposibilidad.

sentence: The analyst broke down the data into three main categories
explanation: 'Break down' significa analizar por partes. Pasado: 'broke down'. Es separable: 'broke the data down' también es correcto.

sentence: If you had backed up your files you would not have lost them
hint: Third conditional: If + past perfect, would have + past participle
explanation: 'Back up' significa hacer una copia. Tercera condicional para situaciones irreales en el pasado.

sentence: The company is phasing out the old software by the end of the year
explanation: 'Phase out' significa dejar de usar algo gradualmente. Es separable: 'phasing the old software out' también es correcto.

sentence: She talked him into applying for the management position
explanation: 'Talk someone into' significa persuadir. 'Into' va seguido de un gerundio.

sentence: They have been putting up with the noise for over a year
explanation: 'Put up with' significa tolerar. Presente perfecto continuo para expresar duración.

sentence: The CEO stepped down after the scandal came to light
explanation: 'Step down' significa renunciar. 'Come to light' significa salir a la luz. Ambos en pasado.

sentence: I wish I had not turned down that job offer last month
hint: Wish + past perfect for past regrets
explanation: 'Turn down' significa rechazar. Es separable: 'turned that job offer down' también es correcto.

sentence: The team came up with a brilliant solution overnight
hint: Subject + phrasal verb + object + time expression
explanation: 'Come up with' significa idear un plan o una solución.

sentence: He thought he could get away with the mistake
hint: Subject + verb + modal + phrasal verb + object
explanation: 'Get away with' significa evitar el castigo o las consecuencias de algo indebido.

sentence: She never looks down on her colleagues
explanation: 'Look down on' significa considerar a alguien inferior.

sentence: Extra training will make up for the lost time
They refused to settle for anything less than the best
hint: Subject + verb + infinitive + phrasal verb + object
explanation: 'Settle for' significa conformarse con algo menos de lo que originalmente se quería.
